dedupe_keys.name: nbsinfra agent based models of nature based solutions for urban resilience generic cologne and prague

description: These three NetLogo 3D agent-based models apply the Resilience and Sustainability Quantification Framework (RSQF) of the EU-funded NBSINFRA project to assess how nature-based solutions (NBS) change urban resilience and sustainability. The generic model represents the built environment, ground, underground and air as static patches and flora, fauna and community members as agents, and evaluates system performance (for example vegetation condition and air quality) and ecosystem service values for NBS types such as rain gardens and bioswales under disruptive events such as rainstorms and droughts, in up to 12 scenarios. The Cologne living lab model covers the Wupper catchment and tests meander reconstruction, revegetation and tree planting under floods and droughts, with attention to soil water retention, biodiversity and socio-economic impacts on urban infrastructure. The Prague living lab model covers the Dejvice university campus and tests green roofs, permeable pavements and bioretention against the urban heat island effect during heatwaves. They were built by Anastasia Tzioutziou at the Aristotle University of Thessaloniki and released on Zenodo on 2 October 2025 as software under CC0 1.0, each as a zip of the GitHub repository (.nlogo3d files and README). Caveats: the repositories are archived, the models are research prototypes with stylised processes, and no calibration data are bundled. They support agent-based climate adaptation and resilience assessment of green-blue infrastructure; a related record is the D4RUNOFF NBS parametric library.
